title: Special Order for Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. — This Special Order ratifies LPSC interventions in Federal Energy Regulatory Proceedings regarding Regional Transmission Organization issues or Entergy Regional State Committee issues.

documents.text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                 SPECIAL ORDER NUMBER 65-2026

                          LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                       EX PARTE

In re: This Special Order ratifies LPSC interventions in Federal Energy Regulatory
Proceedings regarding Regional Transmission Organization issues or Entergy Regional State
Committee issues.

                (Decided at the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                                     ORDER

I.      OVERVIEW

        This matter was on the September 16, 2026 Business and Executive Session (“B&E”)
Agenda for ratification of interventions on behalf of the Louisiana Public Service Commission
(“LPSC” or “Commission”) in Regional Transmission Organization-related or Entergy Regional
State Committee-related (“ERSC”) Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”)
proceedings pursuant to the scope of work approved in connection with the retention of Fishman
Haygood1 and United Professionals Company, LLC (“UPC”) at the February 24, 2021 Business
and Executive Session (“B&E”) for Midcontinent Independent System Operator (“MISO”),
Southwest Power Pool (“SPP”) and ERSC participation. Due to the short deadlines allowed for
these interventions, if advanced Commission approval is not possible, the Executive Secretary on
the recommendation of Staff, UPC or Fishman Haygood, or on his own determination, may
authorize the initial interventions, comments or protests, subject to ratification at a following B&E.
For any pleadings the Commission does not ratify, all work related to such docket shall
immediately cease, and any pleadings filed shall be withdrawn at the direction of the Commission.

        Interventions were filed or plan to be filed on the LPSC’s behalf in the following FERC
dockets: EL26-74, ER26-3169, ER26-3170, CP26-549, AD26-10, ER26-2825, ER26-3248,
ER26-3309, ER26-3426, ER26-3459, and ES26-63.

II.     COMMISSION JURISDICTION AND AUTHORITY

        The jurisdiction of the Commission is set forth by the Louisiana Constitution Article IV,
Section 21, which provides:

                The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
                utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
                It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
                procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
                other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.


1 The Commission originally retained the law firm of Stone Pigman Walther Wittman L.L.C.        At the Commission’s
January 14, 2026 Business and Executive Session, the Commission voted to retain the services of Noel Darce, Dana
Shelton, and Justin Swaim under the currently approved scopes of work, budgets, and hourly rates for all open dockets
to which they are currently hired at the Commission, as well as all dockets the Commission is currently participating
in at FERC as well as to ratify the Executive Secretary’s authorization to transfer all Commission files from the law
firm of Stone Pigman to the law firm of Fishman Haygood.

                                                                                    Special Order No. 65-2026
                                                                                                       Page 1
 III.   CONCLUSION

       This matter was placed on the Commission’s September 16, 2026 B&E Agenda for
ratification by the full Commission. On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice
Chairman Coussan, and unanimously adopted, the Commission voted to ratify the actions taken in
EL26-74, ER26-3169, ER26-3170, CP26-549, AD26-10, ER26-2825, ER26-3248, ER26-3309,
ER26-3426, ER26-3459, and ES26-63.



This Order is effective immediately.




BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
October 7, 2026
